note: Fill the nulls below from the capacity-soak-evidence artifact of one passing 120-minute workflow_dispatch run of app-project-quota-probe.yml (job capacity-soak), started on the branch feat/app-platform-capacity-soak at the reviewed commit with soak_only=true. Nothing here may cite a pull request smoke run: it is five minutes and is never evidence. Until then OPS-08 stays pending and SEC-09 stays partial.

reference_host.volume: 16 GiB XFS project-quota loop volume created and owned by the job

backend_sizing.rule: floor((budget - one minimum backend) / 8), computed from the budgets the runner reports in its readiness facts

load.backend_workload: each backend holds 85% of its memory limit (a Go soft limit at 95% keeps the collector ahead of the kernel), burns its CPU quota, parks threads up to its PID limit minus 8, writes 1 MiB/s to its log and fills its data namespace to ENOSPC; the achieved fractions are measured from each backend's own cgroup counters and recorded, not assumed
load.platform_workload: the relay is driven at the Portal's admission cap of 2 concurrent requests: a flood process outside the measured one keeps one attempt in flight per backend through the Portal HTTP route, at most two are admitted Portal-wide and excess attempts are refused 429 app_platform_busy (about 92% of attempts in the smokes); both counts and every other outcome class are recorded per window. Before the load, a task backlog to the global quota and an event subscription flooded past its in-flight bound
load.batch_workload: the Portal's real batch scheduler (scheduleTick and scheduleLoop) runs against a local stub Dify that answers at once; a standing backlog of 200 queued jobs is held behind long runs that occupy the budget, and a batch job is enqueued every three seconds and given one extra slot; enqueue-to-start latency is measured against the idle baseline with the same bound
load.portal: file-backed SQLite opened with OpenStore; running: the batch scheduler, the relay, installs and uninstalls through the ordinary workers; not exercised: the task worker and event delivery coordinator, a backend-originated message or task request, PostgreSQL

image_beyond_the_image_store.level_note: native when the daemon disk holds two 4 GiB images with 6 GiB of headroom (measured by the job and recorded as image_store_probe and docker_root_free_bytes), else unit level with the measured free space as the reason

layer_beyond_its_declaration.note: the Portal's offline import route; the runner's own refusal of the same bytes is covered by the blob channel unit tests

staging_over_two_gib.note: store level: 384 MiB reservations against the real staging store, the refusal mapped by the real error handler; not driven through the upload route

task_over_installation_quota.note: in-process admitPlatformTask, the function the backend task route calls; the soak backends have no outbound channel

event_subscription_over_quota.expected: review_required:inflight_limit, 64 source events kept, one delivery task

task_over_application_quota.observed_note: not observed in this run: unit level probes record observed null and the tests that prove them, which the job runs

measurements.latency_rule: Owner decision 2026-11-13: the bound is max(1.5x idle p95, idle p95 + 5 ms), measured with load generated outside the measured process. Verdict computation (engineering decision, not the owner's): the pooled loaded p95; per-window p95 are diagnostics

OPS-08.closes_when: a 120-minute dispatch run passes every assertion above

SEC-09.closes_with: OPS-08: the deployed memory, PID, log and storage floods, and the Portal business executor measured by the real batch scheduler's enqueue-to-start latency under the platform load

unproven_until_the_dispatch_run: that p95 of GET /api/home, of the report page, of the queue's dispatch decision and of the batch scheduler's enqueue-to-start latency stay within max(1.5x, +5 ms) of the idle baseline for two hours on shared CI hardware (the verdict is the pooled loaded p95; per-window values are diagnostics)

that the eight backends, held at 85% of their memory and their PID limit less a margin, stay inside the runner's memory and CPU budgets for two hours and none is OOM-killed or restarted, with every backend using at least 70% of its CPU quota in every minute
that the message flood answers requests in every minute at the Portal's admission cap and every other attempt is a typed 429 app_platform_busy
that each refused probe installation releases its namespace through the managed uninstall on the declared 8 GiB disk budget (each probe records retired: managed_uninstall)
the per-application task quota (1000) natively; it is proven at its boundary at unit level only, and the unit tests run in the dispatch job
the task worker and event delivery coordinator under the load, a backend-originated message or task flood, and PostgreSQL: none runs in the soak
